notes.meaning: Jesus came back to Capernaum after traveling and preaching in the country. People quickly spread the news that He was indoors at home, which was likely Simon Peter's house.

A huge crowd gathered so tightly that no one could get in, not even by the front door. Jesus used this chance to preach God's message to them. He cared most of all about feeding their souls with truth.
Four men arrived carrying a paralyzed man on a sleeping mat. The sick man could not walk or help himself, so his friends carried him to Jesus for help.
Because the crowd blocked the way, the men carried the paralyzed man up to the flat roof of the house. They broke open the roof and lowered the man down right in front of Jesus.

Jesus saw the bold, active faith of both the paralyzed man and the friends who brought him. Instead of immediately healing the man's body, Jesus declared that his sins were forgiven. He did this because a person's deepest need is to be made right with God.
Some religious teachers, called scribes, were sitting in the room watching Jesus closely. When they heard what He said, they began arguing silently in their own minds against Him.

The scribes believed Jesus was speaking blasphemy, which means showing disrespect to God by claiming God's own rights. They knew that God alone has the power to wipe away sins. They did not realize that Jesus could forgive sins because He is truly God.
Jesus knew at once in His spirit what the scribes were thinking, even though they had not spoken out loud. He showed His divine knowledge of human hearts by asking why they doubted Him.

Jesus asked them whether it was easier to say sins are forgiven or to tell a paralyzed man to walk. Anyone could claim to forgive sins in secret because no one can see it happen. Doing a visible miracle on the spot was much harder to fake.

Jesus used the title Son of Man to declare His true authority as the Messiah while on earth. He then told the paralyzed man to stand up, pick up his mat, and go home. This visible healing proved that Jesus truly has the power to forgive sins.
The man stood up at once, grabbed his mat, and walked out in front of the whole crowd. The people were filled with wonder and gave praise to God, saying they had never seen anything like it.
Jesus went back out to the shore of the Sea of Galilee, where there was plenty of room for a large gathering. Crowds came out to meet Him, and He taught them the truths of God.

Jesus saw Levi, also called Matthew, sitting at his tax collection booth. Most people despised tax collectors for working with the Roman rulers and taking extra money. Yet Jesus called him to follow Him, and Levi left his business right away to become His disciple.
Levi hosted a large meal at his house so his fellow tax collectors and friends could meet Jesus. Many of these social outcasts came and ate with Jesus and His disciples, eager to hear His teaching.

Jewish religious leaders called Pharisees saw Jesus eating with these outcasts and questioned His disciples. In their culture, sharing a meal showed close friendship and approval, so they thought Jesus was ruining His own holiness.

Jesus explained that healthy people do not need a doctor, but sick people do. He came not to welcome those who proudly think they are already good enough, but to rescue sinners who know they need help.

The Pharisees and the disciples of John the Baptist fasted often, meaning they chose to skip meals for religious devotion. People noticed that Jesus' disciples did not fast like them, so they asked Jesus why His followers seemed less strict.

Jesus answered by comparing Himself to a bridegroom at a wedding feast. Wedding guests do not mourn or skip meals while the groom is celebrating with them. The arrival of Jesus brought a time of great joy, making fasting out of place.
Jesus warned that a time was coming when the bridegroom would be taken away from them. After He was gone, His followers would indeed fast and mourn.

Jesus pointed out that nobody sews a new, unshrunk patch onto an old coat. When the new cloth gets wet and shrinks, it tears away from the weak old cloth and makes an even bigger hole. Jesus did not come merely to patch up old religious routines, but to bring new life.

In Bible times, people kept wine in leather bags that stretched as the wine aged. Putting new, expanding wine into dry, brittle old wineskins would cause the skins to burst and waste the wine. The good news of Jesus brings new spiritual power that cannot be held by rigid old religious traditions.
On the Sabbath, the weekly day of rest, Jesus and His disciples walked through some grainfields. The disciples were hungry, so they picked heads of grain and rubbed them in their hands to eat.

The Pharisees accused the disciples of breaking the Sabbath day of rest. God's law allowed hungry travelers to pick grain from a neighbor's field, but the Pharisees had added strict human rules that treated picking grain like heavy farm labor.

Jesus reminded the Pharisees of Scripture, asking if they remembered what King David did when he and his men were starving. In the time of high priest Abiathar, David entered the house of God and ate the sacred bread, which only priests were normally permitted to eat. Meeting urgent human hunger took priority over ceremonial rules about bread.

Jesus declared that God created the Sabbath to serve and bless mankind, not to make human beings slaves to a day. The day of rest was designed as a gift of mercy and physical relief, never as a harmful burden.

Because the Sabbath was created for mankind, Jesus, the Son of Man, has supreme authority over it. As Lord of the Sabbath, He determines its true meaning and will not let human traditions ruin God's good gift of rest.
